nodes.summary: Let `κ` be an infinite cardinal and `F : ι → Set α` a family of at most `κ` sets, each of cardinality at least `κ`. Then some `B ⊆ α` meets every `F i`, and so does its complement. This is the transfinite construction of Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, hint to Exercise 6A.6 (sets `A_ξ`, `B_ξ` of cardinality `< 2^ℵ₀` built along a well-ordering of the strategies), and of Bernstein's set.
nodes.title: Bernstein-type diagonalisation

nodes.summary: Some `S ⊆ 2^ℕ` is not determined (Gale and Stewart 1953; Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, Exercise 6A.6).
nodes.title: A non-determined game on `{0, 1}`

nodes.summary: If the set of moves `A` is countable and has at least two elements, some payoff set `S ⊆ A^ℕ` is not determined. The proof diagonalises over the continuum many strategies, each of which has continuum many plays (Gale and Stewart, *Infinite games with perfect information*, Ann. of Math. Stud. 28 (1953); Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, Exercise 6A.6, stated there for `A = {0, 1}`). It uses…
nodes.title: Existence of a non-determined game

nodes.summary: Not every `S ⊆ ℕ^ℕ` is determined: the axiom of determinacy AD of Mycielski and Steinhaus is false in Lean's ambient logic, which includes the axiom of choice (Moschovakis, *Descriptive Set Theory*, 2nd ed., AMS 2009, Exercise 6A.6; Woodin, *The continuum hypothesis, Part I*, Notices AMS 48 (2001), section "Determinacy"). The proof only uses a well-ordering of the strategies, that is of the reals.
nodes.title: The axiom of determinacy contradicts choice

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
